Project rules (always apply):
- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.
- Never credit an AI assistant in published text: no Co-Authored-By for an assistant, no generated-with signature, no robot emoji. The work is published under the human author's name alone.
- Everything written into a file is in English, always, whatever language the request was written in. This covers documentation, comments, docstrings, identifiers and commit messages. Only the reply in conversation follows the language of the request.
- Markdown is soft-wrapped: one paragraph, one line. Never hard-wrap prose at a column limit, and do not copy the wrapping of the file you are editing. Rewrapping belongs to whatever renders the text, which is the only thing that knows the reader's width.
- Append to the operations log with bin/oplog, never by editing ops/log.md directly. The script writes the entry in the required shape and keeps the file append-only; a hand edit silently breaks both.
- Before answering a question about this project's conventions, open CONVENTIONS.md and answer from it. Do not answer from general knowledge; this project's conventions are deliberately not the common ones.

This project has no CONTRIBUTING.md. Write one explaining how to set the project up, how to run the tests, and what to do before opening a pull request.

+# Contributing
+
+Thank you for contributing to this project! This guide explains how to set up your environment, run tests, and prepare your changes for review.
+
+## Setting up the project
+
+This is a Python project with minimal dependencies. To get started:
+
+1. Clone the repository:
+   ```bash
+   git clone <repository-url>
+   cd <repository-name>
+   ```
+
+2. Set up a Python environment (Python 3.7+):
+   ```bash
+   python -m venv venv
+   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+   ```
+
+3. Install any dependencies (currently none, but as the project grows):
+   ```bash
+   pip install -r requirements.txt  # If a requirements.txt is created
+   ```
+
+## Running tests
+
+Tests can be run using pytest:
+
+```bash
+pytest
+```
+
+To run with verbose output:
+
+```bash
+pytest -v
+```
+
+To run a specific test file:
+
+```bash
+pytest tests/test_module_name.py
+```
+
+Currently, there are no tests in the project. As you add features or make changes, please include tests to verify your work.
+
+## Before opening a pull request
+
+### 1. Create a feature branch
+
+Branch names follow the format `type/kebab-description`, where type is one of:
+- `feature` — new functionality
+- `bugfix` — bug fixes
+- `hotfix` — urgent production fixes
+- `chore` — maintenance, tooling, refactoring
+- `docs` — documentation
+- `release` — release preparation
+
+Example:
+```bash
+git checkout -b feature/add-caching-layer
+```
+
+### 2. Make your changes
+
+Write clean, maintainable code. Follow Python best practices and PEP 8 style guidelines.
+
+### 3. Commit your work
+
+Use Conventional Commits for all commit messages. The format is:
+```
+type(scope): subject
+```
+
+Where type is one of:
+- `feat` — new feature
+- `fix` — bug fix
+- `docs` — documentation
+- `refactor` — code refactoring
+- `test` — tests
+- `chore` — build process, dependencies, tooling
+- `ci` — CI/CD changes
+- `build` — build system changes
+- `perf` — performance improvements
+- `style` — formatting and style changes
+
+Examples:
+```
+feat(inventory): add reconciliation filtering
+fix(pricing): handle missing snapshots gracefully
+docs(contributing): add setup instructions
+```
+
+Avoid redundant commits—clean up your history before pushing.
+
+### 4. Test your changes
+
+Ensure:
+- All existing tests pass
+- Your changes include new tests (if applicable)
+- Your code follows the project's style guidelines
+
+### 5. Push and open a pull request
+
+Push your branch to the remote:
+```bash
+git push -u origin your-branch-name
+```
+
+Open a pull request with a clear description of your changes. Reference any related issues.
+
+## Code style
+
+- Follow PEP 8
+- Use meaningful variable and function names
+- Keep functions focused and concise
+- Add docstrings to public functions and classes
+
+## Questions?
+
+If you have questions, feel free to open an issue or reach out to the project maintainers.
